name: Warsaw University of Technology
summary: Warsaw technical university, independent since 1915, with over 160 student research groups; 11 English-taught BSc degrees at 9 faculties.

ib.text: Upload your final IB Diploma and results (predicted grades are not accepted; no apostille). Faculties usually look for 70%+ overall with strong maths and science; IB covers English only with English A.

lastYear.text: register 11 May–21 July; documents by 19 August

programmes.name: Architecture
programmes.about: A four-year engineering course in architectural and urban design (IDEAS) at the Faculty of Architecture, with weight on BIM, energy-efficient buildings, daylight and circular-economy design; a master's leads on to a licence.
programmes.overview: The curriculum covers design and planning of urban spaces and architectural volumes, architectural and town-planning theory, history of architecture, fine arts techniques, building economics and investment, design process management with BIM, energy efficiency and circular economy solutions. Most teaching happens in the atelier, where you work under a chosen academic teacher, with unified design seminar blocks in the first four semesters and optional workshops and interdisciplinary seminars in semesters 5 to 8. A preparatory course covers fine art techniques and Polish architecture and culture, and the degree ends with a diploma design thesis presented orally. Graduates work as designers, project managers in building investment, representatives of developers and contractors, or land and real estate consultants; architect licensure follows master-level study.
programmes.ib: An online drawing task (up to 60 points) and an online interview (up to 40) decide admission; registration closes well before IB results.
programmes.selectionNote: A 90-minute drawing task done live online, then an online interview for those who pass it; list Architecture as choice 1. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Electric and Hybrid Vehicles Engineering
programmes.about: Designing, testing and servicing electric and hybrid cars, including autonomous vehicles: powertrain modelling, energy recovery and storage, vehicle structures and mechatronic control, at the Faculty of Automotive and Construction Machinery.
programmes.overview: Modules include mechatronic systems design, sensors and actuators, automation, construction and navigation of autonomous vehicles, ultralight vehicle bodies, crashworthiness, vehicle information systems, energy harvesting, ionics and photovoltaics, diagnosis of electric and hybrid vehicles, advanced control of electric and hybrid drives, and vehicle recycling. Classes and laboratories stress practical work with design and IT tools. You learn to model power train components and to design and test simple multi-source energy storage systems. Graduates can work in the automotive industry on electric and hybrid drives, in machinery sectors, and in transport and energy roles focused on green, energy-efficient technology.
programmes.selectionNote: Faculty reviews your final IB results: it usually looks for 70%+ overall and very good maths and science. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

needs.note: Very good maths and science grades are usually required; no level is stated

programmes.name: Environmental Engineering
programmes.about: Building services (HVAC) and water, sewage, gas and district-heating networks for sustainable, resilient cities; the path leads towards Polish professional construction licences.
programmes.overview: Coursework is grouped into basic sciences, engineering tools (programming, CAD, numerical methods, operations research, AI and GIS), fundamentals of civil engineering, building services and fluid network design, systems modelling and automatic control, and project and investment management. You develop skills in designing building installations such as HVAC, in designing and managing fluid networks, and in water engineering, environmental technologies, the circular economy and the energy transition. The faculty prepares graduates for construction licences in installation, hydrotechnical and structural engineering, with full qualification after a master's degree. Graduates work in water, wastewater, gas and heating infrastructure companies, environmental technology firms, design and consulting offices and technical auditing.
programmes.selectionNote: Faculty reviews your final IB results: it usually looks for 70%+ overall and very good maths and science. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

needs.note: Very good maths and science grades are usually required; no level is stated

programmes.name: Environmental Protection
programmes.about: A new interdisciplinary course on environmental monitoring, modelling and assessment, pollution control and climate neutrality; over 60% of classes are practical, including a project-based module.
programmes.overview: The curriculum is organised in modules on basic sciences, engineering tools (programming, CAD, numerical methods, GIS), law and economics in environmental protection, climate change and air pollution, land surface protection, hydrology and water management, environmental hazards, municipal services and sustainable cities. Specialist strands cover climate neutrality, environmental measurement techniques, and biotechnology with sustainable development. More than 60 percent of classes are practical, including a project-based learning module. Graduates work in environmental consulting and impact assessment, company environmental departments, local and national administration, municipal utilities, planning bodies, site remediation firms and engineering companies.
programmes.selectionNote: Faculty reviews your final IB results: it usually looks for 70%+ overall and very good maths and science. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

needs.note: Very good maths and science grades are usually required; no level is stated

programmes.name: Civil Engineering
programmes.about: Buildings, bridges, roads and railways from design to maintenance, on a base of maths, physics and mechanics; in year 4 you choose a specialisation such as structures, construction management or transport.
programmes.overview: You start with mathematics, physics, mechanics and chemistry, add social sciences and humanities, and move into the core civil engineering areas of structures, surveying, transportation, materials science, management and environment. After year three you choose a specialisation: civil engineering structures, construction engineering and management, energy-saving construction or transportation engineering, with electives such as reinforced concrete and steel structures, renewable energy sources, energy efficiency and cost estimation. An integrated project is available. Graduates take part in the planning, design, construction, operation and maintenance of civil engineering facilities.
programmes.selectionNote: Faculty reviews your final IB results: it usually looks for 70%+ overall and very good maths and science. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

needs.note: Very good maths and science grades are usually required; no level is stated

programmes.name: Electrical Engineering
programmes.about: Circuits, electrical machines, power systems, converter drives and high-voltage technology, with specialisations in control and computer engineering or electrical power engineering.
programmes.overview: The programme covers electrical materials technology, electrical measurements, circuits and systems, the electromagnetic field, electrical machines, electrical power engineering, converter drive control, high voltage technology and IT. Specific modules include CAD methods, electronics, numerical methods, microprocessor engineering, instrumentation and signal transmission, and electric traction. You then follow one of two specialisations: Control and Computer Engineering, or Electrical Power Engineering.
programmes.selectionNote: Faculty reviews your final IB results: it usually looks for 70%+ overall and very good maths and science. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

needs.note: Very good maths and science grades are usually required; no level is stated

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.about: A four-year course at the Faculty of Electronics and Information Technology, specialising in computer systems and networks: algorithms, operating systems, databases, security and software engineering on a two-year ICT common core.
programmes.overview: The first two years are shared with the telecommunications programme and form a common grounding in information and communications technology. Modules include algorithms and programming, circuits and systems, computer systems, telecommunications, operating systems, graphical user interfaces, databases, cryptography and information security, software engineering, compiling techniques and an introduction to artificial intelligence. You work with object programming, CASE-tool-aided design, system analysis, modelling and prototyping, and specialise in computer systems and networks. The aim is to design, implement and operate complex computer systems and networks independently.
programmes.selectionNote: Faculty reviews your final IB results: it usually looks for 70%+ overall and very good maths and science. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

separateFrom.name: Computer Science and Information Systems
separateFrom.reason: A different degree at another faculty (Electronics and IT, 4 years, networks focus) with its own fee; you choose each as a separate IRK option.

programmes.name: Computer Science and Information Systems
programmes.about: Computer science taught at the Faculty of Mathematics and Information Science: three semesters of heavy maths first, then programming, algorithms, networks and AI, with electives from semester 5 and team projects.
programmes.overview: The first three semesters lay a mathematical base, and all students share core courses through semester four: programming in C, C++, Java and C#/.NET, discrete mathematics, algorithms, data structures, operating systems, databases, networks, software engineering, AI, numerical methods, embedded systems and computer graphics. From semester five you choose electives with theoretical and practical emphasis, and the seventh semester is largely given over to team projects and the thesis. Teaching combines lectures, seminars, programming laboratories, team projects and individual thesis work. Graduates can work on IT projects, system verification, and the administration of medium-scale information systems and networks.
programmes.selectionNote: Faculty reviews your final IB results: it usually looks for 70%+ overall and very good maths and science. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

needs.note: Very good maths and science grades are usually required; no level is stated

separateFrom.name: Computer Science
separateFrom.reason: A different degree at another faculty (Mathematics and Information Science, 3.5 years, maths-heavy) with its own fee; you choose each as a separate IRK option.

programmes.name: Mechatronics
programmes.about: Designing mechatronic devices: sensors, drives, microcontrollers and CAD; after semester 4 you choose Mechatronic Devices and Systems or Photonics Engineering (optics, lasers, machine vision).
programmes.overview: The programme covers Matlab programming, 3D CAD, mechatronic drives, theory of machines and mechanisms, microcontrollers, sensors and measuring devices, design of electronic modules, multimedia devices, MEMS and electric metrology. The focus is on practical knowledge of computer design, microprocessor control, drives and actuators, applied to drive systems, measurement devices and automation of manufacturing. Graduates can work in electromechanical and automotive industries, household appliance and machine tool manufacturing, aviation and plants that operate mechatronic systems, or go on to a master's degree.
programmes.selectionNote: Faculty reviews your final IB results: it usually looks for 70%+ overall and very good maths and science. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

needs.note: Very good maths and science grades are usually required; no level is stated

programmes.name: Aerospace Engineering
programmes.about: Aircraft and spacecraft engineering: flight mechanics, aerospace materials, propulsion and rotorcraft, after a first year of maths, physics and mechanics; specialise in propulsion or structures and systems after semester 4.
programmes.overview: The first year builds foundational sciences, the second turns to mechanical design and control engineering, and the third focuses on aerospace topics such as introduction to aerospace, materials in aerospace technology, mechanics of flight, aircraft engine design, aircraft design, aeronautical systems, risk and reliability in aviation and rotorcraft aeromechanics. Design work uses integrated CAD/CAM/CAE systems, and the last half-year is supervised work on the engineering thesis. You choose between two specialisations: Aerospace Propulsion Systems, and Aerospace Structures and Systems. Graduates are prepared for the aerospace industry, airlines, other industries and research institutions working on aircraft and spacecraft.
programmes.selectionNote: Faculty reviews your final IB results: it usually looks for 70%+ overall and very good maths and science. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

needs.note: Very good maths and science grades are usually required; no level is stated

programmes.name: Power Engineering
programmes.about: Thermal and electrical energy systems: thermodynamics, heat transfer, turbines, boilers, heat pumps, renewable sources and power grids, ending with a supervised engineering thesis.
programmes.overview: The first year covers mathematics, physics, mechanics, thermodynamics and computer science, the second adds mechanical design fundamentals and control engineering, and years two and three specialise in thermodynamics and fluid mechanics, heat transfer, electric machines and electronics, combustion and fuels, flow machines, electric power systems, thermal power systems, renewable energy and environmental protection technology. Laboratory work includes measurement and experiment technique, and the final half-year is supervised work on the engineering thesis. Graduates are prepared for industry roles in designing, commissioning and operating power systems, covering energy production, conversion, transmission and distribution.
programmes.selectionNote: Faculty reviews your final IB results: it usually looks for 70%+ overall and very good maths and science. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: EU citizens without Polish citizenship register in the IRK foreigners' branch but pay the EU price in PLN; Electrical, Mechatronics, Aerospace and Power Engineering charge them nothing.
One IRK application takes three programmes in order of priority (fee 85 PLN; Architecture 150 PLN and only as choice 1).
The 2026/27 Senate rules list an online maths and English test for English-taught BSc applicants; ask the International Students Office whether you must sit it.
